newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada decides against higher immigration targets.
newsitem.headline: Canada decides against higher immigration targets.

text.p: The Canadian government announced on Tuesday it would not increase the targeted level of immigration for 1997 because it might not be able to absorb higher numbers.

Citizenship and Immigration Minister Lucienne Robillard said Canada aimed to accept 195,000 to 220,000 people next year, the same range as planned for 1996. She said she expected the actual figure this year to be just over 200,000.
"Immigration is necessary for Canada's growth," she told a news conference.
"At the same time, we must be sensitive to the need to balance our demographic and economic needs with our capacity to settle and absorb immigrants."
The numbers fall short of the 300,000 target the government set in 1994, when it said it would try to let foreigners in at a rate of approximately one percent of the Canadian population each year.
Robillard said she remained committed to that election promise, made "within the limit of our ability to absorb and settle immigrants."
Next year's targets include 168,900 to 187,700 immigrants and 26,100 to 32,300 refugees.
